source_caption:
One of the most beautiful and quietly devastating films about life, family, and the things we never quite understand. Yi Yi follows a middle-class family in Taipei as they navigate love, loss, regret, and the uncertainties of everyday life. Edward Yang captures the beauty and sadness of ordinary moments with such remarkable patience, making even the smallest interactions feel deeply meaningful.

What makes the film so special is its ability to see the world through different perspectives, particularly through a young boy who tries to understand life by showing people the parts of themselves they cannot see. It’s a film that reminds you how little we truly know about the people around us, and how much of life passes by before we realise it.

🎥: Yi Yi (2000)
Dir. Edward Yang

source_details.title: Yi Yi
source_details.synopsis: Yi Yi (Chinese: 一一; pinyin: Yī Yī; lit. 'one one'; subtitled A One and a Two) is a 2000 Taiwanese drama film written and directed by Edward Yang. It centers on the struggles of an engineer, NJ (played by Wu Nien-jen), and three generations of his middle-class Taiwanese family in Taipei. The film's title means "one by one", or "one after another". When written in vertical alignment, the two strokes resemble the character for "two": 二. Yi Yi premiered on May 14, 2000, at the 53rd Cannes Film Festival, where Yang won the Best Director Award. The film has received acclaim and is often regarded as one of the greatest films of the 21st century.
